record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.original_question: Can the random-wave or random-state conjecture for chaotic eigenfunctions be made into a rigorous theorem at microscopic scales, or at intermediate scales between macroscopic size and the wavelength λ^−1? The question asks whether high-energy eigenfunctions ψ_k(x) of chaotic quantum systems have the same statistics as an appropriate random-state ensemble, including value distributions, wavelength-scale correlation functions, nodal sets, and nodal components.

evidence.quote: One would also wish to analyze the wavefunctions ψ k(x) at microscopic scales, or at least some intermediate scale between 1 and the wavelength λ −1.

The main conjecture concerning these microscopic properties is analogous to the BGS conjecture: the eigenfunctions are expected to be statistically equivalent with “random states” in some appropriate ensemble.

The statistical observables to be compared with the random models are manifold. They include the value distribution for {ψ k(x), x ∈ X}, correlation functions at distances ∼ λ −1, the structure of the nodal set {x |ψ k(x) = 0 } and of the complementary nodal components.

To my knowledge, this field of research has mostly consisted in analyzing the properties of the random models, and then numerically checking that these properties are (approximately) satisfied by the eigenstates of some selected quantized chaotic systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary) whose geodesic flow is ergodic (chaotic), and let $\{\psi_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X)$ consisting of eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator, $-\Delta_g \psi_k = \lambda_k^2 \psi_k$, with $\lambda_k \to \infty$. The wavelength of $\psi_k$ is of order $\lambda_k^{-1}$.

For comparison, fix an appropriate "random state" ensemble, e.g.\ Berry's isotropic Gaussian random wave model: a Gaussian field $\Phi_\lambda$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (or its analogue locally on $X$) with covariance kernel given by the spherical average of plane waves of wavenumber $\lambda$, namely
$$\mathbb{E}[\Phi_\lambda(x)\,\Phi_\lambda(y)] = \int_{S^{d-1}} e^{i\lambda \langle \xi, x-y\rangle}\,d\sigma(\xi).$$

Prove or disprove the following random-wave/random-state conjecture at microscopic and intermediate scales: as $k\to\infty$, the local statistics of $\psi_k$ — including
(i) the value distribution of $\psi_k(x)$ for $x \in X$,
(ii) the $n$-point correlation functions of $\psi_k$ at distances of order $\lambda_k^{-1}$,
(iii) the geometry and topology of the nodal set $\{x \in X : \psi_k(x)=0\}$, and
(iv) the statistics of nodal domains (the connected components of $X \setminus \psi_k^{-1}(0)$, including their number, volumes, and topological types) —
agree, in suitable rescaled limits, with the corresponding statistics of the random-wave ensemble $\Phi_\lambda$. The question asks for a rigorous theorem establishing this equivalence at microscopic scales (of order $\lambda_k^{-1}$), or at least at some intermediate scale between the macroscopic size of $X$ and the wavelength $\lambda_k^{-1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The random-wave/Berry conjecture for chaotic eigenfunctions remains broadly open. Partial results exist in arithmetic settings (e.g., Planck-scale mass equidistribution and fourth-moment asymptotics for dihedral Maass forms, results on Eisenstein series and Hecke–Maass forms), but a general rigorous theorem identifying microscopic statistics of chaotic eigenfunctions with a random-wave ensemble has not been established. Recent work notes that the only manifold where local limits of high-energy eigenfunctions are rigorously identified with random waves is the flat torus, which is not chaotic.

status_evidence.title: On the Random Wave Conjecture for Dihedral Maaß Forms
status_evidence.snippet: Two results on arithmetic quantum chaos for dihedral Maass forms... manifestations of Berry's random wave conjecture: Planck scale mass equidistribution and an asymptotic formula for the fourth moment.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the random-wave conjecture is restricted to special arithmetic settings.

status_evidence.title: Local limits of high energy eigenfunctions on integrable billiards
status_evidence.snippet: The only manifold for which the local limits of a sequence of high energy eigenfunctions are rigorously known to be given by random waves is the flat torus, which is certainly not chaotic.
status_evidence.claim: No rigorous random-wave theorem is known for any chaotic manifold.

status_evidence.title: Anatomy of Quantum Chaotic Eigenstates
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describes the conjecture that chaotic eigenstates are statistically equivalent to random states; rigorous results at microscopic scales are essentially absent.
status_evidence.claim: The microscopic random-state conjecture remains a conjecture.
